gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much laptop charge each 25,000 mAh bank delivered on one same test: Macworld's 14-inch MacBook Pro refill score runs from 92% (Anker 25K 165W) to 109% (INIU P63) to 128% (Sharge HyperTower 170) for banks all labelled 25,000 mAh, which at the store prices read 2026-11-26 is $59.30, $61.46 and $99.12 per full MacBook Pro refill.
standout_why: Compared against dupple.com (cited; rated $/Wh at Nov 10 prices, e.g. UGREEN 145W at $79.99 = $0.89/Wh, and it says it prints no measured capacity, recharge time or charge counts), powerbankrank.com (rated price ÷ Wh only, no weight, no measured capacity), and powerbanks.fyi under-$100 and 25,000 mAh pages (mAh, Wh, W, weight, price 'checked Aug 18', no derived figure). Rated $/Wh is therefore already at rivals (that part alone would be 0-1). None of them has a measured refill figure, price per measured refill, measured refill per pound, or recharge hours from the input rating. The TechRadar AU body could not be read (page text truncated before the article), so it is not ruled out. Macworld's roundup, which holds the scores, was not among ChatGPT's results.
decides: It contradicts ChatGPT's line that 'all three have the same advertised capacity, so paying more buys speed or convenience, not more battery life': on Macworld's test the same label delivered 92% to 128% of a 14-inch MacBook Pro. It does not overturn the UGREEN 145W as the price pick ($59.98, $0.67 per rated Wh, the only 140 W port at that price; Baseus FC41 25K is $0.51 per rated Wh through our code), but the UGREEN has no score on that test (Macworld says only that it 'gets very close' to one full 14-inch M2 MacBook Pro). It gives two honest segment winners that are not ours: Sharge HyperTower 170 for most measured laptop charge per charge and per dollar (128%, $59.30 per refill, but 665 g and 100 W max per port), and INIU P63 for most measured charge per pound (126 points per lb at 392 g). Anker 25K 165W at $91.19 is the worst buy on this figure (92%, $99.12 per refill).

It is an earlier revision than the 140 W version sold now, so treat this as a lead rather than a measurement of the current unit.

Baseus EnerFill FC41 25K: weight from Baseus and any named reviewer's measured capacity or laptop refill figure. No Wh per lb or price per measured refill is given for it.
UGREEN Nexode 200W 25K (smart display, the one we link): weight from UGREEN and a measured refill figure. Macworld's 124% is for the different built-in-cable Nexode Pro 25K 200W at $139.99.
A Macworld Test Score or other measured delivered Wh for the current 140 W revision of the UGREEN 145W: Macworld prints no percentage, and Techtest.org's 74-80 Wh is from the 2023 100 W revision.
AOHi Black Warrior: today's store price (storecheck search on aohi.com returned 404, so the desk note of $89.99 was not verified) and any measured capacity. No derived figure is given.
Anker Laptop Power Bank 25K 165W price at anker.com (storecheck search returned 404) or opened at Walmart: the $91.19 used is the figure on Macworld's page.

EcoFlow RAPID Pro 27K (Macworld 120%, 99.54 Wh, 699 g): a maker-store or Amazon price read today. Macworld's page showed $89.99 while Dupple read $175.99 on EcoFlow's store on Nov 10, so no price per refill is given.

Cuktech 15 Ultra and Cuktech 20 25K: Macworld's listing for the 15 Ultra is internally inconsistent (20K in the name, 25000 mAh / 76.56 Wh in the spec), the Cuktech 20 has no printed score, and no US store price was read.
Phone charges per charge: needs a phone battery Wh from the phone's maker, which was not read. ChatGPT's 'three to four charges' is neither confirmed nor corrected.
The Wh that Macworld's Test Score corresponds to (which 14-inch MacBook Pro and its battery Wh from Apple): not stated on the roundup, so scores are left as percentages.
TechRadar AU 'best power banks' article body (cited by ChatGPT): the fetch returned only navigation, so whether it carries measured capacity was not checked.
